## Triage: first grade, `enhancement` · `priority:p3` · `domain:spec` · `area:access`, into `pm:queue`. A package-id arm on the app item read, for `app` only

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-13T06:56Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Unblocks: objectstack-ai/objectui#12285

- **Why p3:** it is objectstack-ai/objectui#12285's wall, and a wall takes the level of the card it blocks. That card shows the wrong verdict screen, with no leak.
- **Lane:** it widens a published door's accept set, so `Clause-②: yes` and spec-lane work, as #12285's grade said.
- **The accept-set choice, made here:**
  - `GET /meta/app/:key` accepts a package id as the key, for `type: app` only. ADR-0048 §3.1 makes the package id the app's routing key under one-app-per-package.
  - The two grammars are disjoint (a snake_case name has no dot; a manifest id has at least one), so the arm is unambiguous.
  - The answer is the same verdict the by-name read gives: 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` for a withheld app, and 404 for no such package app.
  - ⛔ No separate verdict endpoint: one read, not two.
  - ⛔ No other type gains the arm.
- **Disclosure:** a non-holder learns exactly what the by-name read already tells them (the control: `/meta/app/setup` answers 403). Enumeration is no wider, so this does not loosen a boundary.
- **Pins:**
  - a member on a withheld app's package id gets 403;
  - an unknown package id gets 404;
  - a holder is served the app;
  - the by-name read is unchanged;
  - a dotted key on a non-app type is unchanged.
- Triage: lands in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (the request's `name` describe) and `packages/rest`'s item read (`domain:spec`, a cross-lane touch declared in the claim); rationale: the route key answers.

## Regrade: p3 → **p2** · `target:v18` added · a metadata-door widening · triage seat · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-14T07:17Z

**Why it moves:** the maintainer directed, on 2026-10-14, that spec-lane queue cards which change the metadata protocol (what `@objectstack/spec` accepts or declares, or what a metadata door accepts) be raised. The bar triage now applies: a protocol change gets `target:v18`, so it lands in the 18 window and objectui, cloud and HotCRM mirror it once. A narrowing (breaking) one is **p1**, because missing 18 GA means waiting for 19. A widening (additive) one is at least **p2**.

Read fresh. On `main` `b5b1bf7277`, `GetMetaItemRequestSchema` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:351`) keys the item read by `name`, with `packageId` only as a filter. No declared read answers an app's access verdict by its package id.
- **What changes:** the app item read gains the package-id key that my first grade chose (`app` only, with disjoint grammars). That widens a published metadata door's accept set.
- **Why the 18 window:** objectstack-ai/objectui#12285 waits on it (`Unblocks:` stands), and objectui's 18.x mirror can then take it in one move.

## Regrade: p2 → **p1** · metadata-protocol change, the objectui-dependency rule · triage seat · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-14T07:45Z

**Why it moves to p1:** the maintainer added, on 2026-10-14, 「协议变更还经常会影响 objectui 项目的开发，相关任务经常等 spec 发版本」. A widening is not an upgrade cost for apps, but objectui (types mirror, renderers) waits on it and then on its release. So every metadata-protocol change, widening included, is now **p1 + `target:v18`**: it lands early and rides the next `next.N` cut.
- **Consumer waiting:** objectstack-ai/objectui#12285 is `pm:blocked` on this card.
